artworks.description: A sculpted white marble fountain by Olivotti & Co. with a shallow, gadrooned bowl resting on a bulbous fluted & stop-fluted pedestal with a square concave-sided base carved with foliage and resting on claw feet. artworks.title: "Homage to Alexander"
artworks.description:
An early seventeenth century historical tapestry entitled “Homage to Alexander” after a design by and woven at the workshop of Karel van Mander II (Dutch, 1579-1623). It is one of nine allegorical tapestries based on the life of Alexander the Great by van Mander. The wool and silk tapestry is woven in bright colors and depicts the presentation of the daughters of King Darius III of Persia to the victorious Alexander. Alexander stands to the left of center as two nobles bow before him, one of whom hold the leash of a monkey drinking out of a fountain in the foreground. Behind the noblemen are the huddled Persian Princesses. The entire scene is enclosed by a wide border of vines in tones of brown, green, gold, and red, a narrow stylized inner border is inscribed at center “MANDER FECIT ANNO 1619.”

Agents of Cornelius Vanderbilt II acquired the tapestry in 1880 at an auction in Florence, Italy. Prior to Vanderbilt this tapestry formed part of the famed collection of Prince Anatole Demidoff (Russian, 1812-1870). The tapestry was stored at the Vanderbilt’s New York townhouse until moved to Newport and incorporated in the construction of their new summer villa The Breakers. When installed by Jules Allard at the landing of the grand staircase the tapestry’s top and bottom borders were folded under and velvet side panels added to extend the tapestry’s width in order to fit the space of the bracketed wall panel.
artworks.credit: Gift of Countess Nandine Eltz, 1974.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Great Hall: 50 feet high, the grand staircase and the stair-landing tapestry
artworks.placeNote: Hung by Allard on the landing of the grand staircase (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection).

artworks.title: Louis XIV Ormolu-mounted Ebonized Clock with Gallic Rooster
artworks.artist: André-Charles Bouller (attributed), Jules Allard et ses Fils
artworks.dimensions: H 93.5 inches · W 21 inches · D 11.75 inches
artworks.description: A Louis XIV ormolu-mounted ebonized and blue-died horn, brown tortoiseshell, ebony and brass premiere and contrepartie boulle marquetry regulateur (tall case clock) attributed to workshop of André Charles Boulle. The carcass largely early 18th century, with modificationsand later partial mounting done in London during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Hood mount of infant boy with Gallic cock by Jules Allard et ses Fils. The movement signed on the reverse "Archard/70. Soh. Audley St./London."
artworks.credit: Partial gift of Loyd-Paxton, Dallas, partial PSNC purchase, 2007.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Great Hall: 50 feet high, the grand staircase and the stair-landing tapestry
artworks.placeNote: Stood in the Great Hall from 1926 to 1973 and came back in 2007 (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection); that it is in the Great Hall today is our guess.

artworks.title: Cast Iron Fireback
artworks.dimensions: H 48 inches · W 58 inches
artworks.description: A cast iron fireback from the workshop of Jules Allard and Sons, installed in the Great Hall fireplace of The Breakers. The rectangular fire back has an arched crest and a border with lotus leaf tips. Depicted in relief at center is the Vanderbilt coat of arms, featuring three acorn sprays on the right of an armorial shield. The shield is crested by a helmet with a barred visor and surrounded by a foliate mantel featuring bulrushes, ribbon, stylized flowerheads and acanthus leaves.
artworks.credit: Gift of Mrs. Gladys T. Peterson, 1972.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Great Hall: 50 feet high, the grand staircase and the stair-landing tapestry
artworks.placeNote: In the Great Hall fireplace (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection).

artworks.title: Napoleon III Style Upholstered Bench
artworks.dimensions: H 22 1/2 inches · W 94 1/4 inches · D 31 1/4 inches
artworks.description: A Napoleon III style upholstered bench with three loose cushions made by William Baumgarten & Co., NY, designed by Emile Baumgarten (American, 1865-1922) for use in The Breakers Billiard Room. The bench and cushions are upholstered in green velvet, the corners of the bench are decorated with gold tassels, and the seat rail is trimmed with green and gold braid. The bench is raised on turned mahogany legs joined by stretchers and supports a mahogany footrest at the front.
artworks.credit: Gift of Countess Anthony Szapáry, 1974.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Billiard Room: gray-green marble, alabaster and mosaics; its 1895 furniture
artworks.placeNote: Made for the Billiard Room (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection).

artworks.title: Carved Mahogany Occasional Table
artworks.dimensions: H 25 3/4 inches · W 26 inches · D 26 inches
artworks.description: An occasional table of carved mahogany made by William Baumgarten & Co., NY, designed by Emile Baumgarten (American, 1865-1922) for use in The Breakers Billiard Room. The table has a circular top with a raised molded edge. The top rests on three fluted columnar supports and a central spirally turned bulbous column. These stand on a shaped triangular base raised on three ball and claw legs.
artworks.credit: Gift of Countess Anthony Szapáry, 1974.

artworks.title: Mahogany Pedestal Writing Table
artworks.dimensions: H 30 1/4 inches · W 60 3/4 inches · D 37 1/2 inches
artworks.description: A mahogany pedestal writing table made by William Baumgarten & Co., NY, designed by Emile Baumgarten (American, 1865-1922) for use in The Breakers Billiard Room. The rectangular top is lined with a panel of green baize, has rounded corners, and a molded border. The front of the desk has a frieze containing three drawers with brass drop front handles, below this are two cupboards joined by a molded stretcher along the bottom. The four outer corners of the writing table are carved with monopodium lions, the inner corners are carved with columns with elaborate capitals and pendant fruiting foliage suspended from bow-knotted ribbons. The outer sides of the table are carved with central egg and dart circular medallions and spandrels. The cupboard doors are framed with a rectangular egg and dart border. The whole stands on eight bun feet.
artworks.credit: Gift of Countess Anthony Szapáry, 1974.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Billiard Room: gray-green marble, alabaster and mosaics; its 1895 furniture
artworks.placeNote: Made for the Billiard Room (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection).

artworks.title: Mahogany Billiard Cue Rack
artworks.dimensions: H 90 inches · W 26 1/2 inches · D 26 1/2 inches
artworks.description: A billiard cue rack composed out of carved mahogany, made by William Baumgarten & Co., NY, designed by Emile Baumgarten (American, 1865-1922) for use in The Breakers Billiard Room. The circular revolving cue rack is supported by a central fluted column topped by a flambeau finial and carved on the lower portion with foliage. The cue rack stands on a block pedestal base with a central cabinet. The top of the base has a rounded molded edge, the body is carved with monopodium lion corners, the sides are carved with egg and dart spandrels and circular panels, the whole stands on four bun feet.

artworks.title: Carved Mahogany Billiard Marker
artworks.dimensions: H 71 inches · W 32 inches · D 18 inches
artworks.description: A billiard marker (or score keeper) of carved mahogany made by William Baumgarten & Co., NY, designed by Emile Baumgarten (American, 1865-1922) for use in The Breakers Billiard Room. The upper portion is of abacus form with two double rows of red and white beads used for keeping score. The frame is surmounted by scrolled cresting carved with foliage forms and a central flambeau finial. The upper portion rotates on a turned baluster pedestal with a gadrooned top and carved foliage around the bottom. This is raised on a concave-sided triangular base with paneled sides and three paw feet with carved foliage above.

artworks.title: Steinway Model B Grand Piano
artworks.dimensions: H 39 inches · W 59 inches · D 83 inches
artworks.description: A Steinway Model B grand piano. The iron-framed instrument is contained in an ebonized wooden case and stands on three heavy turned and fluted legs raised on casters. Printed in gold on the front of the piano is “Steinway & Sons. / Patent Grand. / New York. / London. [picture of the lyre trademark] Hamburg.” The interior is marked with the serial number 81767. Purchased from Steinway & Sons by Cornelius Vanderbilt II in July 1895.

artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County

artworks.placeNote: The family’s Steinway, delivered June 1895 (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection); that it stands in the Music Room is our guess.

artworks.title: Carved Oak Extending Dining Table
artworks.dimensions: H 29 1/4 inches · W 79 inches · D 79 inches · [Diam] · L · [Remarks]Unextended
artworks.description: A carved oak extending dining table from the workshops of Jules Allard and Sons for use in the Dining Room at The Breakers. The rectangular quartered top is outlined with broad banding of lemonwood between bandings of purpleheart and has a molded edge. Below the edge of the table top is an ovolo frieze with carved fruiting foliage. The table is supported by massive end supports in the form of back-to-back figures flanking a gadrooned baluster column highlighted with gilding, below is a swag of fruiting foliage held in the mouth of two lion masks, the end supports end in trestle feet. A center stretcher supports a large bulbous baluster column with gilded leaves around the base. Together with seven extra leaves the table extends to sit thirty four people.
artworks.credit: Gift of Mrs. Gladys T. Peterson, 1973.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Dining Room: two storeys high, alabaster columns, two Baccarat crystal chandeliers
artworks.placeNote: Made for the Dining Room; with its seven leaves it seats 34 (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection).

artworks.title: 'Pierre de Tonnerre' Chimney Piece
artworks.dimensions: H 168 inches · W 144 inches
artworks.description: A Francois I limestone "pierre de Tonnerre" chimney piece original to the chateau of Arnay-le-Duc (Cote d' Or) in Burgundy, France. The pilasters, surround, and frieze are carved with finely detailed tendrils, flowers, cherubs and garlands of fruit, and the hood is carved with four large circular relief roundels separated by slender, bombé colonettes each depicting a theme from "The Legend of Orpheus," from left to right: Orpheus on Earth, playing his lyre enchanting humans and beasts, Orpheus presiding over athletes and warriors, and Orpheus in the underworld pleading with Pluto and Prosperine for the release of his dead love Eurydice, while holding a lyre on one knee. Roundels shallowly inscribed with the "MB" Merlan de Beaumont family cypher and at base of colonettes, and inscribed in old French: "de gran bien me rie/et poinct ne default/ Il n' est qu' adresse quant tout prevault "Little do I care for riches/and little are they missed/ since only cleverness prevails in the end". Both inscriptions are 19th century embellishments.
artworks.credit: Purchased by The Preservation Society of Newport County, 1973.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Library: walnut, gilded leather and a 16th-century French chimneypiece
artworks.placeNote: The Library’s chimneypiece: descriptions of the Library quote its Old French motto, “Little do I care for riches” (Wikipedia, The Breakers).

artworks.title: “Portrait of Gertrude Vanderbilt”
artworks.artist: Raimundo de Madrazo y Garretta, Thomas A. Wilmurt (framer)
artworks.dimensions: H 58 3/8 inches · W 39 1/4 inches · D · [Diam] · L · [Remarks]Unframed
artworks.description:
Oil on canvas “Portrait of Gertrude Vanderbilt” by Raimundo de Madrazo Y Garreta (Spanish, 1841-1920). The portrait depicts Gertrude Vanderbilt (1875-1942) at age five, she is shown at full length seated on a giltwood stool, posed against a backdrop of lush blue drapery, with her feet crossed and perched upon a pillow. She wears a frilled white dress with a pink satin sash tied around her mid-section and black boots. The canvas is signed and dated on the upper right corner and is housed in its original carved giltwood frame. The elaborate frame is decorated with an egg-and-dart molded border crested by a bow-knotted floral wreath with cascading floral garlands. 

Gertrude sat for the portrait during a family visit to Paris. That same summer, Madrazo also painted a portrait of her mother Alice Claypoole Gwynne Vanderbilt (1845-1934) (PSNC.8112). The painting formerly hung in Cornelius Vanderbilt, II's New York City residence at 1 West 57th Street.
artworks.credit: Purchased by The Preservation Society of Newport County, 2021.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Gertrude Vanderbilt’s Bedroom: the eldest daughter, later the sculptor Gertrude Vanderbilt Whitney
artworks.placeNote: A portrait of Gertrude Vanderbilt as a girl; that it hangs in her bedroom is our guess.

artworks.title: Portrait of Cornelius Vanderbilt II
artworks.dimensions: H 30 inches · W 23 inches
artworks.description: An 1890 oil on canvas portrait study of Cornelius Vanderbilt II (1843-1899) by John Singer Sargent. The portrait depicts New York Central railroad heir Cornelius Vanderbilt II bust-length in a black day suit against a neutral ground, his right hand tucked into his jacket. Mr. Vanderbilt, his mother and siblings commissioned thirteen portraits from Sargent between 1888 and 1906.
artworks.credit: Purchased by the Preservation Society of Newport County, 2009.

artworks.galleryName: Mr. Vanderbilt’s Bedroom: Cornelius Vanderbilt II
artworks.placeNote: Sargent’s study of Cornelius Vanderbilt II; that it hangs in his bedroom is our guess.

artworks.title: Portrait of Mr. Cornelius Vanderbilt II
artworks.dimensions: H 32 inches · W 26 inches
artworks.description: A portrait of Mr. Cornelius Vanderbilt, II by Benjamin Curtis Porter (American, 1843-1908). The subject, Cornelius Vanderbilt II (American, 1843-1899), is depicted at half-length against a dark background, his body is turned slightly to the right, and he looks straight at the viewer. He wears a dark suit with a white high collar shirt. The canvas is signed and dated on the bottom right corner.
